newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain has to go on reducing deficit - BoS Rojo.
newsitem.headline: Spain has to go on reducing deficit - BoS Rojo.

text.p: Bank of Spain Governor Luis Angel Rojo said on Tuesday that it was reasonable that the Spanish consumer price index end the year at 3.4 percent and said it was essential that Spain continue cutting the budget deficit in years ahead.
He was speaking before the budget commitee of the legislature.
"It is fundamental that (Spain) continue to reduce the public deficit coming years because this is going to be the general approach," Rojo said.
Rojo said also that in coming months doubts are likely to emerge on the markets about "the sustainability of the convergence process" of European Monetary Union (EMU).

This is the reason why it is crucial to make bigger reductions in public deficits. To strengthen the credibility of fiscal convergence, a stability pact will likely be agreed with a three year-time horizon among the countries in the single currency.
Rojo also said that it is reasonable to close the year with a CPI at 3.4 percent year-on-year, with a yearly average of 3.6 percent.
"This is reasonable and it is not optimistic", Rojo said.
Spanish CPI moderated to 3.6 percent in September down from 3.7 percent.
